questions.question: What can happen when you drink alcohol while taking drugs?

options.text: The effects of both drugs and alcohol become weaker.
The effects of both drugs and alcohol become stronger.
It will help cure your illness.
It will improve your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both drugs and alcohol become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can make both substances stronger in your body. It is unsafe to drive after using either alcohol or drugs alone. It is even more dangerous to drive after using them together.

questions.question: Which sign shows a driver may be drunk?

options.text: The driver is weaving between lanes.
The driver is going slower than other traffic.
The driver is stopping suddenly and quickly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include weaving between lanes, driving faster or slower than other traffic, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: When pulled over by police, what documents must a driver show?

options.text: Proof of insurance.
A driver's license.
Proof of vehicle registration.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Drivers must carry and show their driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. All three documents must be in the vehicle at all times when driving.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady green traffic light?

options.text: Continue driving unless there are vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving unless there are vehicles or pedestrians in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles still in the intersection. You can continue, but slow down if the light might change before you reach the intersection.

questions.question: What happens when drivers eat or drink while driving?

options.text: They make no driving errors.
They have trouble driving slowly.
They become better drivers because they are not hungry.
They have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These activities take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things are more likely to drift between lanes and lose control of their vehicle.

questions.question: How can stress affect your driving?

options.text: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
It decreases your chances of having an accident.
It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
It makes you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lowers your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Strong emotions can hurt your driving ability. Worry, anger, fear, excitement, or sadness can lower your concentration. If you feel emotionally upset, wait before driving to keep yourself and others safe.

questions.question: Who should wear a seat belt?

options.text: Only the driver.
Passengers only on long drives.
All occupants on expressways only.
All occupants every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: All occupants every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in the car should wear a seat belt at all times. In a crash, a person without a seat belt becomes a flying object that can harm everyone in the vehicle.

questions.question: Which substances can impair your driving and result in a DUII arrest?

options.text: Beer, wine, and other liquor
Illegal drugs and prescription medicines
Inhalants like glue or paint
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair driving. These include all types of alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications such as prescription and over-the-counter drugs.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches up.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. Pull over to the right edge of the road when you see flashing lights or hear a siren. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: When must you use a turn signal?

options.text: Only in city traffic.
Only when traffic is behind your vehicle.
Only when other vehicles are in sight.
When changing lanes or turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: When changing lanes or turning.
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Use it for a longer distance if you are driving at high speed.

questions.question: You must signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb:

options.text: Only if other cars are nearby.
It is required by law and a safe driving habit.
Only while you are making the move, not before.
Not if you are driving slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is required by law and a safe driving habit.
questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn or change lanes. The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before moving your car right or left. Always signal before pulling away from a curb so other drivers know your plans.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than other cars.
Drive at the speed limit.
Slow down.
Stay close behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When rain reduces how far you can see, drive slower. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see clearly, pull to the side of the road and stop until it improves.

questions.question: Smoking while driving is:

options.text: Not a problem for your driving.
Helpful because it keeps you alert.
A distraction that takes your focus away from driving.
Not a distraction.

questions.correctAnswerText: A distraction that takes your focus away from driving.
questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is dangerous because it takes your hands off the steering wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: You had a difficult time at work and feel angry. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play loud music so you do not think about it.
Drive fast on the highway to release your anger.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Stop at a bar and drink before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, take time to calm down before driving. Driving while angry is dangerous and puts you and others at risk.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 lbs. are allowed.
A steep hill is ahead.
A truck stop is ahead.
Trucks are not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: What does an orange sign with black letters mean?

options.text: Stop.
No turning.
Roadwork is happening.
Yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Roadwork is happening.
questions.explanation: Construction zone signs are diamond-shaped and orange with black letters. Be extra careful when you see these signs.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Left turns are not allowed.
A traffic worker is ahead.
Two-way left turn allowed.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left turns are not allowed.
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must do. This sign means you cannot make a left turn.

questions.question: The best way to prevent hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Avoid standing water and puddles.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet roads make cars take longer to stop and easier to skid. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: You arrive at an intersection with no signs or signals at the same time as a car to your right. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and let the car on your right go first.
Drive through and make the other car stop.
Honk your horn and drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the car on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two cars arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the car on the right has the right-of-way. Wait for that car to pass safely before you go.

questions.question: What can happen when you mix alcohol with another drug?

options.text: Both drugs become stronger.
Nothing will happen.
Both drugs become weaker.
Only the alcohol becomes weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both drugs become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug makes both effects stronger. For example, having one drink while taking a cold medicine can affect you like you had several drinks.
